top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one identifiable idea, the magic-wavelength condition that cancels the trapping Stark shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once. It has been reproduced at the 1e-18 level in several laboratories and already feeds clock comparisons, relativistic geodesy, tests of varying constants and preparation for a new SI second. A two-name credit to Katori (concept) and Ye (record-accuracy development) is defensible, and a citation naming the lattice clock draws a clear line against the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. I still rate topological insulators higher on conceptual novelty, but that case is not on the slate and its credit is more disputed. A prize this year is better than no award.
